The series has an unstable ranking (ranking_tau=0.025), which makes fixed weights risky. However, simple averaging (mean) often outperforms DBA in noisy, low-predictability regimes because it maximizes diversification across the many weak but complementary signals present here. I will test a simple mean combination of the top models to see if robustness beats the specific optimization of DBA.

The current leader (a2) uses a simple mean on a small, specific pool (pool4). Given the "unstable" ranking and "noisy" regime, I need to test if expanding the pool to include models from different correlation groups (like NaiveMovingAverage which was best in window 1, and catboost which was best in window 2) with inverse error weighting improves robustness. The hint suggests that complementary models can help even if individually weaker.
Test complementarity of trend (catboost) and naive/seasonal (NMA) models with the top mean pool.

The leader (a4) uses a simple mean on a small pool (pool5). The series has unstable ranking and noisy characteristics, suggesting that robust aggregation methods like trimmed_mean or median might be more effective than a plain mean. I will test trimmed_mean on the top 5 models to see if removing outliers improves performance given the low predictability and potential for divergent forecasts in this noisy regime.

The ranking is unstable (ranking_tau=0.025) and the series is noisy, suggesting that a robust combination like trimmed_mean on a focused pool is superior to simple mean or weighted averages which may be sensitive to outlier errors. I have already tested trimmed_mean on pool5. I will now test a broader robust combination using the full pool with a wider trim (30%) to further mitigate the impact of poorly performing models in this noisy regime, leveraging the "robust" hint from the decision card.

The current leader (a5) uses a trimmed mean on a small, selected pool (pool5). Given the unstable ranking and noisy regime, I need to test if expanding the pool to include more diverse models (redundant but potentially complementary) helps, while maintaining robustness. I will try a trimmed mean on the full pool to see if the larger diversity outweighs the noise of weaker models, or if the previous small-pool approach was superior due to outlier rejection.

The current leader (a5) uses a trimmed mean on a small, heterogeneous pool (ARIMA, ETS, catboost, FT_rf, NaiveMovingAverage). The series has unstable rankings and low predictability, making robust aggregation key. I want to test if including the trend-champion ONLY_CWT_catboost alongside the seasonal/naive models improves performance, potentially using a weighted combination that accounts for the varying reliability across the recent windows.

The current leader (trimmed_mean on top-5) benefits from robustness to the unstable ranking (tau=0.025). I will test a different robust combination method, median, on the same high-performing subset (pool5) to see if it handles the noise better than the trimmed mean.

The leader (a5) uses a trimmed mean on a small pool (top 5). The series has low predictability and unstable rankings, suggesting that robust aggregation is key. I will test a broader pool (top 7) with a trimmed mean to see if including slightly weaker models helps while still mitigating outliers, or if the tighter pool is superior due to noise.

The series has unstable rankings and low predictability, suggesting robust aggregation over a small pool of complementary models is optimal (leader a5 used trimmed_mean on top 5). I will test if expanding the pool to include more independent variance sources (pool8) improves performance compared to the tight pool5.

The current leader (a5) uses a trimmed mean on a small, tight pool of 5 models. To test robustness against this specific "robust combination" hypothesis in a noisy, unstable ranking regime, I will now test a simple mean over the full stable top-k pool to see if expanding the diversity slightly without trimming helps or hurts compared to the focused trimmed approach.

decision.justification: Selected 'trimmed_mean on pool5' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9226. Series context: trend strength 0.5255 and seasonal strength 0.1706; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.025); 3 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.431.
